summary:
This project is a multi-stage interactive simulation of NASA's Artemis Mission, built using the Godot Engine. It guides players through sequential chapters: suiting up, launching aboard Orion via the SLS rocket, enduring deep-space microgravity transit, and executing the final Human Landing System descent onto the lunar south pole.
Transforming complex orbital mechanics into intuitive, hands-on gameplay, the project solves the challenge of abstract space logistics. It serves as an engaging, lightweight educational tool designed to boost STEM interest and inspire a new generation of space explorers.
details:
1. Project Details
* What it does & how it works: Built in the Godot Engine, this interactive simulation recreates NASA's Artemis Mission in sequential playable stages—from suiting up in crew quarters and boarding the Orion spacecraft for launch, to managing microgravity life in deep space and landing on the lunar south pole.
* Benefits & Expected Impact: It transforms abstract aerospace theories into hands-on gameplay, serving as an engaging classroom tool that sparks student interest in STEM and deep-space exploration.
* Tools, Languages & Hardware: Developed using Godot Engine (GDScript) for game mechanics and scene transitions, Blender/Tinkercad for 3D assets, and standard desktop PC hardware.
* Innovation: Unlike passive videos, it breaks an interplanetary mission into interactive chapters featuring custom microgravity physics and spacecraft control panels.
* Factors Considered: The team prioritized scientific accuracy (matching real Artemis flight phases), smooth UI/UX navigation, and performance optimization for standard student computers.
2. Project Summary
This project is a multi-stage interactive simulation built in the Godot Engine that models NASA's Artemis Mission. Players progress through distinct mission chapters: equipping space suits during pre-launch, boarding the Orion capsule for rocket liftoff, experiencing microgravity life during lunar transit, and executing the final descent onto the Moon's south pole. It solves the challenge of visualizing complex orbital mechanics and spaceflight logistics by turning them into accessible, hands-on gameplay. Ultimately, it matters because it inspires curiosity in space exploration and provides an effective, interactive STEM learning resource for students.
